q: Do voltage optimisers or servo stabilisers really cut electricity and emissions?
title: Voltage optimisers: real savings?
short: Only for loads that use less power at lower voltage, such as some lighting and resistive heaters. Motors on drives, LED drivers and electronics often save little. A stabiliser also has its own losses. Measure kWh with the unit bypassed and in service before counting any saving.

ul: Lightly loaded motors without drives, sometimes.
LED drivers and electronics with regulated supplies.
Heaters on thermostats, which simply run longer.

p: Alternate weeks with the unit in service and bypassed at similar production, and compare kWh per unit made. Count only a measured saving, multiplied by 0.710.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
